title: "Open Problems in Indirect Treatment Comparisons"
subtitle: "An audited catalog of what is actually unsolved in ITC and population-adjusted indirect comparison methodology"
toc: false
---

The field is not short of estimators. It is short of identification discipline, estimand
discipline, target-population discipline, and diagnostics that expose how much of an answer is
supplied by data rather than by assumption.

This site catalogs the open problems, one entry at a time. Each says what the problem is, why
it stays open, what has already been tried, and the most probable route to a solution.

## The organizing distinction

The decisive division in this field is **anchored versus unanchored evidence**, not matching
versus regression versus multilevel modeling.

In an anchored comparison, randomization still identifies the within-trial relative effect, and
population adjustment is mainly about transporting effect modification. In an unanchored or
disconnected comparison, the analyst has to reconstruct a causal contrast across studies: every
prognostic factor and effect modifier that creates cross-study outcome differences becomes
relevant, and residual confounding is generally not testable. Most of the hardest entries in
this catalog live on the unanchored side of that line.

Three consequences run through the whole collection:

**Adjustment to one trial population is not transport to the decision population.** Pairwise
matching and regression approaches usually target the population of the trial that supplied
aggregate data. Applying that effect to a reimbursement population is a second transport step,
and it is commonly hidden.

**Weak overlap is not a nuisance diagnostic; it changes the scientific question.** When weights
are extreme or a model extrapolates beyond its support, the nominal target estimand may cease
to be credibly identified. Reporting an effective sample size does not repair that.

**In a disconnected network, some assumption carries the information across the gap.** Baseline
risk, a dose-response curve, a treatment class, a shared component — each answers a different
question and imports different bias. That software produced a connected posterior is not
evidence that the effect is identified.

## Reading a verdict

Every entry carries a verdict recording what happened when its claims were checked against the
literature and against two independent external auditors. A verdict of
[Overstated]{.verdict .verdict-overstated} does not mean the problem is not real; it usually
means the underlying issue is real and a claim about its severity was pitched too strongly.
Entries marked [Resolved since report]{.verdict .verdict-resolved-since-report} are kept rather
than deleted, because knowing that something was recently closed is as useful as knowing it is
open.

The source material for this catalog was produced by a large language model and then audited.
[How this was verified](methods.qmd) explains what that means in practice, including where the
audit's own limits are.
